To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
working at home can have a negative impact on workers' mental and/or physical health.

the mental and physical health of employees who work from home is strongly influenced by the availability of organizational support, colleague support, and levels of work-family conflict, and that women are less likely to experience positive outcomes when working from home than are men.
working at home is associated with both positive and negative effects on workers' health and that these outcomes vary according to gender and the degree of organisality support.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to optimise health whilst working at-home (WAH) and the role of the work environment in this process.
the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on working at home.
the impact of working at home (WaH) on the health and well-being of workers, and the factors that influence this impact.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
WAH is not necessarily detrimental to health, but that there is a risk of detrimental health effects if WAH is not well managed.
WAH has both positive and negative impacts on mental and physical health and these impacts are influenced by a range of factors.
there are no clear benefits or disadvantages to working at home for individual workers' mental or physical health.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
working at home is not necessarily detrimental to workers' mental or physical health.
working from home can be beneficial to the individual worker's health, but this will depend upon the individual's work and home circumstances.
the health of WAH workers can be optimised with the right work environment and support.
The main takeaway from our work is that
organisations need to be mindful of the impact of WA.
WAH can impact on health outcomes and this impact will vary between individuals and organisations.
organisations should consider the impact of the organisational context on workers' health and well being.
